ev.q: Eight cases of autochthonous malaria were reported to CDC by state health departments in Florida (seven) and Texas (one) during May 18–July 17, 2023.
All patients reported fever, six reported chills, five reported abdominal pain, and five reported vomiting.
Seven of the eight patients were hospitalized, none developed severe malaria, and no deaths were reported.
As of August 4, a total of 407 Anopheles mosquitoes have been tested.

public_health_question.v: What were the characteristics of, and public health response to, the first autochthonous P. vivax malaria cases in the United States since 2003?

ev.q: triggering an investigation into the first mosquito-transmitted (i.e., autochthonous) malaria case in the United States since 2003
Outbreak of Locally Acquired Mosquito-Transmitted (Autochthonous) Malaria — Florida and Texas, May–July 2023
This outbreak report does not include the recent locally acquired case of P. falciparum malaria
On May 17, 2023, enhanced case finding through syndromic surveillance was initiated
All seven cases were reported by the providers to the county health department
TDSHS successfully contacted three of the four persons to ascertain clinical details and recommend malaria testing
requested telediagnosis assistance from DPDx, CDC’s interactive parasitic diseases website
All seven reported Florida cases occurred in persons who lived within a 4-mile (6.4-km) radius in Sarasota County.

equity.level_reason: Homelessness (SES, housing status) appears only as a descriptor of three Florida patients and in outreach; age and sex are table counts only.

level_alternative.reason: Homelessness of individual cases in a small series could be read as a clinical descriptor only, leaving only age and sex counts.

ev.q: Three of the patients in Florida reported experiencing homelessness.
FDOH collaborated with organizations serving unhoused persons in the area and provided insect repellent, bed nets

equity.equity_measurement: Homelessness reported for 3 of 7 Florida patients and used as a syndromic surveillance search term; no group comparison.

notes: Descriptive case series of 8 cases nested in an outbreak investigation; mosquito testing counts (407 Florida, 71 Texas) are reported without comparison. Laboratory methods (PCR, RDT, smear, G6PD assays) confirm case status and are not procedures.
